1) the -2708G>A, -629C>A, -971G>A and +784CCC>A polymorphisms are associated with CETP and HDL-C levels in CAD males; 2) haplotype analysis indicates that -629C>A is the functional polymorphism that determines CETP and HDC levels and that -2708G> A and -971G>A are likely to play an important role in determining CET P levels; and, 3) a
the -629C--> A promoter polymorphism is independently associated with plasma CETPs concentration and HDL-cholesterol, whereas the TaqIB intron 1 polymorphism is not.
the TaqIB variant in intron 3 of the CETP is not associated with CETP or HDLC, but is a genetic marker for the -2708, +784 and -629 variants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic variants that determine CETP concentration, and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the associations of these variants with plasma lipids and CAD.
the identification of functional polymorphisms in the CETP gene, and the elucidation of their role in the determination of CETP and HDL-C levels.
the identification of genetic factors that are involved in the regulation of the cholesterylester transfer protein gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CETP gene contains at least three independent functional polymorphisms, -629, -2708 and possibly -971, which are involved in determining CETP and HDL-C levels.
-629 and -2708 are independently associated with plasma CETPs and HDL-C concentrations.
the CETP gene is not a monogenic gene, but that the regulation of CETP gene expression is the result of complex interactions between multiple polymorphisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CETP gene contains several functional polymorphisms, and that the TaqIB variant is a marker for -2708, the -629 promoter mutation and -971, which are likely to contribute to CETP concentration and, thereby, HDL-C.
the TaqIB and -629 polymorphisms are independently associated with plasma CETPs, but that -629 is the most relevant functional polymorphism.
the TaqIB and -629 polymorphisms are the only ones that are independently associated with plasma lipids, and that these associations are not mediated by the CETP concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
haplotype analysis is an important tool for identifying functional sites in the CETP gene.
the -629 promoter polymorphism is a functional variant, which is in line with the recent finding that the -629C-->T promoter variant is associated with CAD.
a haplotype approach is a powerful tool for the dissection of complex genetic traits.
